stage1_evidence_shown.label: PURPOSE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To provide insight into the factors by which obesity in itself may directly lead to early arterial damage, we aimed to determine early sonographic markers of obesity-related vascular dysfunction in young obese males.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Thirty-five young obese males and 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers were recruited into the study. Common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were calculated from blood flow velocities curves obtained by pulsed Doppler ultrasonography.

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"maybe","confidence":0.5,"reason_for_action":"The study describes measuring carotid pulsatility and resistance in young obese males vs controls but provides no outcome data here, so available evidence is insufficient to confirm or refute."}

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: The mean pulsatility index, resistance index, body mass index, waist circumference, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, homeostasis model assessment for insulin resistance, plasma fasting glucose, insulin, C-peptide, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein were statistically higher in obese subjects than in healthy controls.
